However, we only list Cat S or N cars as Cat A and B cars are not roadworthy and safe. Category S (formerly Category C) The 'S' in Cat S stands for structural damage. This means the vehicle has damage to its structure/chassis, which is more than just cosmetic damage. But the vehicle can be professionally repaired, making it safe and roadworthy. Category N (formerly Category D) Similarly, the 'N' in Cat N stands for non-structural damage. Here, the vehicle has sustained damage, but it has not affected the structure/chassis. A Cat N car is safe to drive as the damage could be minimal/cosmetic. Buying a written-off vehicle: Do a full vehicle history check to identify category vehicles.
